audit.whatIsWrong: The chart itself is already correct and matches the mirror (Urgot / Urgot / Skill / Urgot / Skill / Urgot / Urgot in both layers), but five of the seven whys and the whole mid paragraph argue the opposite — 'Levels 2-6 are firmly Cassiopeia's'. A reader sees Urgot on the row and Cassiopeia in the sentence under it.
audit.why: The mirror set this chart deliberately with Level 3 and Level 6 as the two contested stages, and the 54.81% win rate supports it. The prose was never brought along.
audit.corrected: whys[1] through whys[5] and mid rewritten to argue the chart they sit on. No chart rows touched — they already agree with the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: Miasma is the tracked cooldown on every screen and its duration is never given; nor is Petrifying Gaze's.
audit.why: Miasma is 24s at rank 1 — that gap is the entire matchup, because it is the only window in which Disdain works. Petrifying Gaze is 120s, Noxious Blast 3.5s, Twin Fang 0.75s.
audit.corrected: 24s, 120s, 3.5s and 0.75s written into the spikes, mid, cooldowns and dos.

audit.whatIsWrong: The grounding interaction is stated correctly but with no timing attached, and Twin Fang's healing is missing entirely. late also credits Corrosive Charge with shred.
audit.why: Riot: Miasma grounds and grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities — that is what kills Disdain. Twin Fang deals increased damage to poisoned targets and heals her for a percentage of it, so she wins every long trade without Grievous Wounds. Corrosive Charge deals physical damage and slows.
audit.corrected: Grounding tied to Miasma's 24s window as the sequencing, Grievous Wounds written into spikes[2], the shred claim replaced with the slow.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cassiopeia is called 'he' and 'him' in tldr, winCon, report[0], report[1], report[8], report[11] and dontsFull[2].
audit.why: Same voice defect the mirror flagged on the other side.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed in every affected string.

edits.before: Cassiopeia poke-dominates this phase: her Q puddle and W Miasma grounding stop your E dash entirely, so if she lands W on you, you cannot Disdain in — walk out of the poison first and only step up when W is down.
edits.after: Miasma is the whole matchup: 24s at rank 1, and while you stand in it the grounding kills Disdain outright — walk out of the poison before you commit. Noxious Blast is only 3.5s, so eat that chip and step up in the W gap.

edits.before: Her R Petrifying Gaze stuns you if you face her, so at 6 the ranged fight is still hers; turn your back to break the stun into a slow, but respect that she out-pokes and grounds you all game.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze stuns only enemies facing her — turn your back and it is just a slow. At 120s rank 1, once she spends it the level-6 window is yours: Disdain in behind the shield, then R her low.

edits.before: With her first item Cassiopeia's E spam and mana sustain let her chunk you repeatedly while grounding your E, so farm patiently, build MR/HP, and wait for the level where your bulk out-scales her poke.
edits.after: With her first item Twin Fang fires every 0.75s and heals her off the damage, so buy Grievous Wounds alongside the MR and HP — without it she wins every long trade even while you win the short ones.

edits.before: Levels 2-6 are firmly Cassiopeia's — her W grounds your E so you cannot engage, and her Q/E poke plus R stun let her kite you the entire laning phase while chipping you down.
edits.after: Levels 2-6 hinge on Miasma: 24s at rank 1, and while it is on you Disdain is dead, so walk out of the poison first. In the gap between casts you step up and Purge wins the trade outright.

edits.before: You finally take over with items: build HP/MR, and once your bulk survives her burst, Corrosive Charge shred and R execute end her the moment her grounding is down and you're on top of her.
edits.after: You take over with items: build HP/MR, and once your bulk survives her burst, Corrosive Charge's slow and the R execute end her the moment the grounding is down and you are on top of her.

notes: The chart on this page already matched the mirror, so I changed no rows — the defect was that five whys and the mid paragraph argued the opposite of the rows they label. The packet's own defect note complains the chart gives Cassiopeia 5/7 stages; that describes the packet's chart, not the one on disk, which is fine. Per the mirror's finding I did not restore any percent-max-health claim for Purge — Riot's text for Echoing Flames and Purge says physical damage and nothing else.
